senses.definition: The hollow bed of running waters; (also) the bed of the sea or other body of water.
examples: The water coming out of the waterwheel created a standing wave in the channel.

senses.definition: The natural or man-made deeper course through a reef, bar, bay, or any shallow body of water.
examples: A channel was dredged to allow ocean-going vessels to reach the city.

quotes.text: European adventurers found themselves within a watery world, a tapestry of streams, channels, wetlands, lakes and lush riparian meadows enriched by floodwaters from the Mississippi River.

senses.definition: The navigable part of a river.
examples: We were careful to keep our boat in the channel.

senses.definition: A narrow body of water between two land masses.
examples: The English Channel lies between France and England.

quotes.text: Our citizens and our businesses on both sides of the channel need more security and predictability for the future
quotes.reference: 2018 May 14, Jon Stone in Brussels, The Independent:

senses.definition: Something through which another thing passes; a means of conveying or transmitting.
examples: The news was conveyed to us by different channels.

quotes.text: But I write to tell you what you will hear through all the various channels by which news travels,...

senses.definition: (biochemistry) An ion channel: pore-forming proteins located in a cell membrane that allow specific ions to pass through.
A gutter; a groove, as in a fluted column.
(construction, mechanical engineering) A structural member with a cross section shaped like a squared-off letter C.

quotes.text: The channel is not very efficient as a beam or column when used alone, but built-up members may be constructed of channels assembled together with other structural shapes and connected by rivets or welds.
quotes.reference: 1960, “Structural Shapes”, in Construction Materials, Concrete Construction, and Engineer Computations, U.S. Government Printing Office:

senses.definition: (electronics) A connection between initiating and terminating nodes of a circuit.
examples: The guard-rail provided the channel between the downed wire and the tree.

senses.definition: (electronics) The narrow conducting portion of a MOSFET transistor.
(communication) The part that connects a data source to a data sink.
(communication) A path for conveying electrical or electromagnetic signals, usually distinguished from other parallel paths.
examples: We are using one of the 24 channels.

senses.definition: (communication) A single path provided by a transmission medium via physical separation, such as by multipair cable.
examples: The channel is created by bonding the signals from these four pairs.

senses.definition: (communication) A single path provided by a transmission medium via spectral or protocol separation, such as by frequency or time-division multiplexing.
examples: Their call is being carried on channel 6 of the T-1 line.

senses.definition: (broadcasting) A specific radio frequency or band of frequencies, usually in conjunction with a predetermined letter, number, or codeword, and allocated by international agreement.
examples: KNDD is the channel at 107.7 MHz in Seattle.

senses.definition: (broadcasting) A specific radio frequency or band of frequencies used for transmitting television.
examples: NBC is on channel 11 in San Jose.

2008, Lou Schuler, "Foreward", in Nate Green, Built for Show, page xi
TV back then was five channels (three networks, PBS, and an independent station that ran I Love Lucy reruns), […]

senses.definition: (storage) The portion of a storage medium, such as a track or a band, that is accessible to a given reading or writing station or head.
examples: This chip in this disk drive is the channel device.

senses.definition: The part of a turbine pump where the pressure is built up.
examples: The liquid is pressurized in the lateral channel.

senses.definition: (business, marketing) A distribution channel.
(Internet) A particular area for conversations on an IRC or similar network, analogous to a chat room and often dedicated to a specific topic.

quotes.text: The excerpt in Figure 1 below shows a list of some channel names as they appear to an IRC user. senses.definition: (Internet, historical) A means of delivering up-to-date Internet content via a push mechanism.

(transitive) To make or cut a channel or groove in.
(transitive) To direct or guide along a desired course.
examples: We will channel the traffic to the left with these cones.

senses.definition: (transitive, of a spirit, as of a dead person) To serve as a medium for.
examples: She was channeling the spirit of her late husband, Seth.

senses.definition: (transitive) To follow as a model, especially in a performance.
examples: He was trying to channel President Reagan, but the audience wasn't buying it.

senses.definition: (nautical) The wale of a sailing ship which projects beyond the gunwale and to which the shrouds attach via the chains. One of the flat ledges of heavy plank bolted edgewise to the outside of a vessel, to increase the spread of the shrouds and carry them clear of the bulwarks.
